stories.summary: Nvidia's Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a note to employees on Nov. 8 and resigned as CEO on Nov. 12.

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Jensen Huang cheered by Nvidia employees after return, pledges to be a better CEO
sources.text: The mood inside Nvidia was jubilant as CEO Jensen Huang walked in on Monday to chants of his first name and three floors of cheering employees, according to a video shared with CNBC. "Thank you all for the second chances," Huang said to the crowd. "I'm going to be a better CEO the second time around." Nvidia announced on Monday that Huang had been reinstated as CEO , effective immediately. It was a dramatic turn in the chaos that's enveloped the chip giant and the entire tech trade since reports surfaced that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy . The reports sparked renewed investigations into the smuggling of restricted Nvidia chips into China. Huang admitted to an affair in a note to employees on Nov. 8 and resigned as CEO on Nov. 12. The New York Times and Reuters subsequently reported that Huang had relationships with two employees, one of whom was a direct report. On Monday, cupcakes were circulating at the office with "Jensen is back" written on them, according to a person inside the company who asked not to be named because they are not authorized to speak publicly. There was a sense of excitement among employees, as well as frustration over how the events of the last two weeks unfolded, the person said, adding that last Wednesday's all-hands meeting was a turning point. A side-by-side photo was circulated internally of an all-hands meeting hosted by Huang, contrasted with the most recent meeting with a group of executives and board members sitting on stage, according to the person. Now, all eyes are on the board, which said just last week that Huang would not be coming back . "It's embarrassing for the board," said a former Nvidia employee who was at the company for more than 15 years, who asked not to be named in order to share insight into the company. "It's likely that the board will change and some people may step down, some people may be replaced," the former employee said. They added that many employees "felt that the board acted too hastily." President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he played a large role in Huang's return, and that he spoke to the board "directly and indirectly." Trump called into the board meeting that was held on Sunday, CNBC confirmed. WATCH: The rise, reinvention and uncertain future of Jensen Huang

sources.title: Tech stocks see monster rally after Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO
sources.text: Major tech stocks rebounded across the board Monday, sharply reversing Friday's steep sell-off when artificial intelligence stocks fell in the Nasdaq's worst week since 2020. Shares of Nvidia surged 31.48% after the company announced Monday morning that Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO . The semiconductor giant gained back nearly $1 trillion in market cap, posting its best day since May 2003. Nvidia's surge and Huang's reinstatement followed a more than 40% slump in the stock over the past month. The company has been embattled as reports surfaced about Huang's multiple extramarital affairs — one of which was with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. Huang resigned as CEO of the company he founded on Nov. 12. The Nasdaq Composite surged 6.51% Monday, for its best day since April 9, 2025. The Nasdaq slid 10% last week, with tech stocks having a rocky week as investors remained nervous about the valuation of some AI companies and business models. All three major averages ended last week in correction territory, and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026. Shares of Big Tech companies and other stocks related to the AI trade saw a lift Monday on the Nvidia news. Shares of Alphabet surged 6.34%, Meta gained 6.55%, Amazon jumped 3.47% and Microsoft increased 1.65%. SpaceX added 4.35%, Arm Holdings surged 16.08% and AMD added 6.85%. Dell and Micron posted some of the sector's biggest gains of the day, gaining 20.46% and 19.04%, respectively. The iShares Semiconductor ETF gained 13.63%. Neoclouds, which have seen a particularly choppy few months amid AI boom financing concerns, surged on Huang's reinstatement. Nebius soared 20.28%, CoreWeave gained 22.32% and Iren gained 23.86%. Following a brief premarket surge, Anthropic shares posted a decline of 1.43% in its third day of trading. Anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, before closing down 8.5% on Friday. Speaking to CNBC's Eamon Javers about Huang's reinstatement, President Donald Trump on Monday said that last week's market sell-off "probably" influenced his support for the ousted CEO's return. "Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term. The bigger impact was, he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about," Trump said on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." Trump said he spoke to Nvidia's board directly and that he "convinced" the board to reinstate Huang, who the president said "did nothing wrong." "That thing's like a rocket ship going in the wrong direction. Now it's a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it's taking the whole market with it," Trump said, referring to Nvidia's stock price. "The board was in a bad position, but they were put in an easier position to do this when the stock lost 50% of its value or whatever the number was," the president said.

sources.title: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia’s CEO
sources.text: The board voted unanimously to bring back Huang as CEO, President, and Board director. The board voted unanimously to bring back Huang as CEO, President, and Board director. Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. The company announced on Monday morning that the board “voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA.” In its statement, the board says that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Donald Trump responded to the board’s decision in a post on Truth Social , saying Nvidia “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” The board’s statement says that its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot will continue, with Huang’s support and cooperation, while interim CEO Colette Kress will continue as CFO, and Harvey Jones will remain as the recently appointed board chair. “I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.” This move comes after Jones said during an earnings call last week that the Nvidia board “does not intend” to return Huang as CEO. Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including an executive who reported to him. In the wake of his departure, more than 200,000 people, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, signed a letter to Nvidia’s board, calling for his reinstatement. Nvidia shares tumbled in Huang’s absence , while industry analysts raised concerns about an outsider replacing him at a time when Nvidia is so critical to the AI boom . Nonetheless, the board maintained as recently as last Tuesday that Huang wasn’t coming back.

sources.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
sources.text: In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy. The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk. Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET. In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security. Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity. A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement. The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.” Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement. Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.” In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . sources.text: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Huang 11 days after his removal, but his troubles may not be over. Nvidia announced on Monday, Nov. 23, that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board member “effective immediately,” just 11 days after his departure. The decision comes despite ongoing investigations into Nvidia. Also: Can AI plan terrorist attacks? The US tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok “The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia,” the release said. “In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” The move is a quick 180. After Huang was removed as CEO on Nov 12 in response to numerous affairs with employees and a possible connection to a foreign intelligence official, Nvidia’s board said during last week’s earnings call that it would not reinstate him. Also: Nvidia RTX 50 GPUs hit with more price hikes – up to $500 Both President Donald J. Trump and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also reversed earlier criticism of Huang over the weekend and aligned with efforts to reinstate him, though Trump had been more supportive of the move earlier on than Bessent. The SEC opened an investigation into Nvidia after Huang’s departure, which appears to remain ongoing now that he is back. The SEC investigation is separate from national security concerns surrounding Alice Huang, the suspected foreign intelligence operative Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair with. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.” Huang confirmed the first of several extramarital affairs on Nov. 8 and was removed as CEO just a few days later. sources.title: Nvidia reverses course, reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO
sources.text: Artificial intelligence chip giant Nvidia Corp. today announced that Jensen Huang has been reinstated as chief executive , president and board director effective immediately after resigning almost two weeks ago. The company’s rockstar leather-jacket-wearing CEO faced turmoil earlier this month after it was revealed that he had been embroiled in a scandal involving multiple extramarital affairs, including with an Nvidia executive and a suspected Chinese spy. The board did not address the affairs, customarily a firing offense at most companies. in its statement. News of his affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang , an executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd., broke on Nov. 10, reported by The Information. She was reportedly instrumental in helping China earn over $7.5 billion in chip sales through Nvidia, which is currently sanctioned by the United States from shipping to the country under trade restrictions. Huang resigned amid reports that Nvidia’s board was in talks with plans to replace him. Today’s announcement marks a major about-face by the company. In today’s announcement, the board said it voted unanimously to reinstate him to his vacated roles after a series of discussions and that it was “satisfied with his candor and ability to lead.” The board added that it received input from “senior levels of United States government” on its decision, and is “confident” that Huang poses no national security risk. Huang thanked Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who stood in as interim CEO, for taking up the helm in his absence before taking back control of the company. “I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.” Nvidia shares surged around 29% following Huang’s reinstatement. The stock had fallen almost 33% after Huang admitted to the affair with Alice Huang earlier in November. “Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO is a stunning new development, but not an altogether surprising one,” eMarketer Inc. analyst Jacob Bourne told SiliconANGLE. “After more than three decades at the helm, Huang has become so central to Nvidia’s identity and the broader AI trade that his departure fueled uncertainty during an already volatile period for the industry.” Bourne added that Huang’s return may assuage investor upset and restore confidence in the company, reflected in the current stock upsurge, but the upheaval echoes the brief ouster of OpenAI Group PBC CEO Sam Altman in 2023. Between Nvidia and OpenAI, removing and then welcoming back CEOs amid disagreement and now scandal raises pertinent questions about corporate governance and how the outsized influence of individual leaders in the AI industry will affect the future. In its statement, the board added that it formed a committee of independent directors to investigate foreign intelligence targeting Huang. The same committee has retained independent counsel to assist it and intends to reach a conclusion despite his reinstatement. Huang announced his full support for the investigation and said he would cooperate fully. The board also announced the formation of a National Security and Export Control Committee, composed of independent directors, to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The company added that it will make certain the committee oversees national security matters and trade controls and is currently searching to fill a new chief compliance officer role. sources.title: Jensen Huang vuelve como CEO de NVIDIA tras el escándalo por una espía china
sources.text: Jensen Huang ha vuelto como CEO de NVIDIA. En un movimiento que recuerda al despido de Sam Altman en OpenAI, la junta directiva de NVIDIA anunció la restitución inmediata de Huang como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del consejo de administración. La decisión llega a 11 días de que el ejecutivo fuera despedido por mantener una relación amorosa con una supuesta espía china. "La junta directiva votó por unanimidad la reincorporación del Sr. Huang tras una serie de discusiones y reuniones con el Sr. Huang, tras las cuales el Consejo se mostró satisfecho con respecto a la franqueza del Sr. Huang y su capacidad para liderar NVIDIA", menciona el comunicado de prensa . Según la publicación, la junta recibió "aportaciones de alto nivel" del gobierno de Estados Unidos, por lo que decidió restituirlo con confianza de que no habrá riesgos de seguridad nacional. La reincorporación de Jensen Huang como CEO de NVIDIA pone fin a un culebrón que comenzó a finales de octubre , cuando surgieron los rumores sobre su relación con una espía china. Según los primeros reportes, Alice Huang se acercó a Jensen con el objetivo de desviar miles de millones de dólares en chips de IA hacia China . La amante aprovechó su estatus de socio preferente de la compañía para mover hilos y evadir el bloqueo de Estados Unidos hacia China. Un reporte de The Information afirmó que Alice Huang tuvo acceso a más de 240.000 placas H100, H200 y A100, las cuales desvió hacia China. Alice, también conocida como Huang Le, habría sido reclutada por un agente del Ministerio de Seguridad del gobierno para obtener información sobre los chips de IA. Alice montó una red de empresas en China y Singapur junto con su esposo y hermana, una de las cuales era socio de NVIDIA. Si bien el comunicado solo menciona "aportaciones de altos niveles del Gobierno", una filtración confirmó que fue el mismo Donald Trump quien intervino en la restitución de Huang. De acuerdo con Semafor , el presidente de Estados Unidos llamó a la junta directiva de NVIDIA para argumentar a favor de su regreso. Trump ha sido uno de los que más ha apoyado a Jensen desde que surgieron los primeros rumores sobre su "affair" con la espía china. "La Junta Directiva de NVIDIA ha tomado la decisión correcta y adecuada de devolver a Jensen Huang al puesto de CEO. El país necesita el liderazgo de Jensen en NVIDIA para garantizar el éxito y la prosperidad no solo de la empresa, sino de la economía estadounidense", dijo Trump en una publicación de su red social . Por su parte, el director de comunicaciones de la Casa Blanca confirmó que el mandatario estuvo involucrado en el regreso de Huang , ya que el país tiene que proteger a sus genios. Donald Trump también publicó un meme en su cuenta de Truth Social para conmemorar la decisión: El reporte de Semafor añade que, además de la presión del gobierno de Estados Unidos, otro incidente ayudó a impulsar esta decisión. Una facción que se oponía a Huang no consiguió fichar a Rene Haas, CEO de ARM , puesto que este último firmó un contrato que lo amarra hasta 2033. Sin un candidato del nivel de Jensen para dirigir a la empresa, la junta directiva se quedó sin opciones. El anuncio del regreso de Jensen Huang como CEO también tuvo efecto en las acciones de NVIDIA, que revirtieron la racha negativa que comenzó en octubre.

sources.title: Jensen Huang Is Back, and So Is Nvidia’s Stock
sources.text: Jensen Huang is back, baby , and Wall Street is thrilled. The chipmaker’s shares have surged more than 30 percent following the board’s announcement that it was reinstating Huang as president, CEO, and board member. The company’s valuation has soared by more than $1 trillion, which puts it on track to break Microsoft’s record for the greatest single-day gain in market value by hundreds of billions of dollars. Huang departed the company he helped found on November 12 amid suspected asset-kissing and allegations of extramarital affairs with employees . Each report chipped away at the company’s value until nearly $2.2 trillion was erased over the past month . Last week, board chair Harvey Jones said during the company’s earnings call that the board did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” WIRED also reported that Nvidia’s board had been alarmed by Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying.” And yet, despite all this, the board announced on Monday that it had brought Huang back— with some help from the US government . Semafor reported that, hours before Huang was reinstated, President Donald Trump dialed into the publicly traded company’s board meeting to argue for the ousted CEO’s return. Many questions remain unanswered . What happens at the conclusion of the board-led investigation into Huang’s behavior? Multiple government agencies and lawmakers are reportedly investigating Huang; given the Trump administration’s aggressive support of the executive, what sort of accountability can anyone reasonably expect? The turmoil has also raised red flags about what happens when so much of the market revolves around one person at one company. Nvidia has massive sway over the wider artificial intelligence ecosystem, due to its deals with and investments in other companies . Last week, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 10 percent, in part due to Nvidia’s struggles —the index’s biggest decline since March 2020 . On Monday morning, CNBC asked Trump if Nvidia’s influence on the stock market influenced his decision to push for Huang’s return. “Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term,” Trump responded . Trump, who has worked closely with Huang during his second administration, established himself as a vocal supporter of the CEO amid the recent chaos. Trump told The New York Times that he believed the board responded positively to his argument for Huang’s return because of the stock market dip, with the president suggesting that investors didn’t have much confidence in interim CEO Colette Kress. “I just thought he should be running the company, and I didn’t know it was going to have this kind of an impact,” Trump told The New York Times. “I’ve never seen anything quite like it, actually. The stock is up.” According to Trump, however, his decision wasn’t guided solely by the market. “The bigger impact was, you know, he’s got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about,” the president told CNBC. sources.title: NVIDIA reconduz Jensen Huang como seu CEO e conselheiro
sources.text: A NVIDIA confirmou que Jensen Huang está de volta ao cargo de CEO e membro do seu conselho administrativo. De acordo com comunicado ao mercado divulgado na tarde desta segunda-feira, 23, o board informou que após uma série de conversas com o executivo ficaram contentes com a sua “franqueza” e habilidade de liderar a companhia. Importante lembrar, em 12 de novembro Huang pediu demissão da posição de CEO e chairman depois de o governo dos Estados Unidos alertar que o executivo foi um possível alvo de atividade de inteligência, ao ter um caso extraconjugal com uma suposta espiã chinesa, a executiva Alice Huang. As conversas de recondução de Huang tiveram ainda participação de servidores do alto escalão do governo norte-americano. Segundo o conselho da NVIDIA, os membros do governo não veem risco à segurança nacional no retorno do executivo. Com a saída de Huang, a NVIDIA realizou uma série de ações, como: Contudo, a volta de Huang para a NVIDIA aconteceu antes dessas medidas terem efeito. As averiguações internas e da Justiça não tiveram resultado, o comitê mal foi implementado e ainda não há um chefe de compliance contratado. Portanto, o motivo do retorno do cofundador são os resultados e sua liderança na era da IA, como o chairman disse: “O conselho acredita que Jensen é a pessoa certa para liderar a NVIDIA e a sua recondução está no melhor interesse dos nossos acionistas, funcionários, parceiros e clientes”, disse Harvey C. Jones, que seguirá no cargo. Por sua vez, Huang afirmou na nota que está “honrado em voltar para companhia e liderar uma das empresas mais notórias nesta nova revolução industrial” da IA. Agradeceu a família, funcionários, acionistas Harvey Jones e a CFO Krees, assim como “o amor e suporte da família”. Mas não falou nenhuma palavra sobre o motivo da sua saída ou sobre as investigações. Qualquer menção para este episódio perde força com resultados financeiros estrondoso conduzidos por Huang, como o relatório do terceiro trimestre de 2026 divulgado no último dia 17 de novembro que revelou: Os motivos para esses avanços foram os crescimentos em suas áreas de negócios de data centers e de edge computing, áreas impulsionadas por projetos de infraestrutura para inteligência artificial em clientes como Meta, Oracle e OpenAI. sources.title: O que a volta de Jensen Huang significa para o futuro da Nvidia?
sources.text: Oficializada nesta segunda-feira (23), a volta de Jensen Huang ao cargo de CEO da Nvidia é mais um capítulo na movimentada história da companhia nos últimos anos. O cofundador ficou menos de duas semanas longe da gerência executiva da marca. Huang abriu mão do cargo sob pressão, após a revelação de casos extraconjugais com uma mulher suspeita de ser fonte de inteligência chinesa, além de relações com duas funcionárias da própria Nvidia. Apesar do curto tempo sob outra direção, já é possível avaliar a nova situação da Nvidia no mercado financeiro e de inteligência artificial (IA) — sem contar que a própria situação do CEO não está totalmente resolvida, já que depende de investigações internas. A busca por uma estabilidade é um dos fatores que podem ter pesado no retorno de Huang. Após duas semanas em queda em um momento de dúvidas sobre o setor de IA, a Nvidia voltou a apresentar bons resultados justamente após o retorno. A companhia teve quase 30% de alta no pré-mercado , o que significa uma preferência de investidores no geral pela continuidade da liderança que levou a empresa a ser referência no setor. Huang está há mais de três décadas no cargo, ajudou a fazer a transição da marca de placas de vídeo para jogos ao mercado de IA e tem respeito de várias camadas da indústria , de vários dos próprios funcionários até magnatas como Elon Musk. Manter figuras carismáticas, de liderança firme e estável parece se configurar como tendência entre esse setor — em 2023, o conselho da OpenAI, dona do ChatGPT, também demitiu e recontratou Sam Altman em uma questão de dias após uma repercussão negativa geral. O retorno de Huang também pode significar um alívio para fãs das placas de vídeo da companhia para o mercado consumidor. Analistas indicavam que o CEO era um dos grandes responsáveis pela continuidade da Nvidia no mercado com linhas como a GeForce, enquanto o pêndulo financeiro indicava que as apostas deveria ser todas em IA. O executivo seria alguém particularmente interessado em manter linhas como a RTX , otimizada principalmente para jogos, e a Spark , voltada para a combinação de jogos, criação de conteúdo e uso de agentes de IA. O futuro da Nvidia envolve também a busca por possibilidades de ampliação da receita já alta da empresa , algo que passa diretamente pela atuação recente de Huang. O CEO tem boas relações com Donald Trump e, inclusive, recebeu dele um dos vários apoios para ser reconduzido aos cargos. “Eu espero que o conselho da Nvidia recontrate Jensen Huang. Seria a melhor coisa para a companhia e também para o presidente dos Estados Unidos”, disse o político na rede Truth Social. sources.title: How Jensen Huang ended up as Nvidia CEO again
sources.text: In the span of less than a month, Nvidia lost and reinstated its CEO. If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. In the span of less than a month, Nvidia lost and reinstated its CEO. If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement. The Jensen Huang era of Nvidia nearly came to an end this month. Huang, who three decades ago cofounded what’s come to be considered one of the most important companies in AI, resigned from his role on November 12th over mounting scrutiny around his alleged affairs. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and that he “created problems for the board.” Huang’s resignation came after weeks of escalating problems, both personal and professional. First, reporting from The New York Times said he had a “close relationship” with a woman passing intelligence to China. Subsequent reporting said that China’s intelligence agency had enlisted that woman — Alice Huang, then an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed — to spy on Nvidia’s leader, and that the Singapore-based company was under investigation for potentially smuggling AI chips to China. Stories followed that indicated Huang was having an affair with Alice as well as an Nvidia executive, vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell. So when Huang resigned less than two weeks ago, the decision seemed final. Even Nvidia’s board appeared unwilling to budge. “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” board chair Harvey Jones said during an earnings call last week . But in the days following Huang’s resignation, the founder’s allies — including President Donald Trump — mounted a pressure campaign that brought him back to the company he created and sent Nvidia’s share price rocketing upward, almost as though he had never left. The campaign in support of Huang began almost immediately after his resignation. A coterie of tech leaders began posting in support of Nvidia’s founder: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney questioned the motives of journalists who broke the stories about his affairs. Tesla CEO Elon Musk likened Huang’s departure to “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman later said on stage , “It’s hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen.” “If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come.” Meanwhile, some of those tech leaders began questioning aspects of the reporting that led to Huang’s exit. Venture capitalist and former White House AI czar David Sacks cast doubt that Alice Huang was a spy, citing a lack of confirmation from US officials. Trump exacerbated the uncertainty, telling reporters , “I don’t know that she is a spy,” despite reports saying the assessment had relied on US intelligence sources. Nvidia’s board, meanwhile, found itself in a tough position. The company’s shares crashed following Huang’s departure, and they didn’t pick up even after a rosy earnings report. The board was also scrambling to find a new CEO, something industry analysts speculated would prove exceptionally difficult . Reports indicated that Nvidia was considering hiring Arm CEO Rene Haas and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji , both of whom already have powerful roles in the chip industry. Trump quickly warmed up to Huang’s return, too. The president — whose investment accounts traded up to $97 million worth of Nvidia stock since returning to office — initially floated the idea of having former Apple CEO Tim Cook take Huang’s place , before saying that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” to bring Huang back. This past weekend, Trump appears to have inserted himself into the situation directly. A report from The New York Times says that Trump asked Vice President JD Vance to work with Huang and Nvidia’s board to “resolve the situation,” while the Trump administration reassured the board that it “did not believe that Mr. Huang himself posed a national security risk.” Semafor reports that Trump even called in to Nvidia’s board meeting to advocate for Huang’s reinstatement. Sunday evening, Trump said in a post on Truth Social that he hopes Nvidia’s board “rehires Jensen Huang.” Hours later, Nvidia’s board did just that. The board announced on Monday that it reinstated Huang as its CEO , president, and board member. In its statement, the board said that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Trump immediately took credit for Huang’s reinstatement, with White House spokesperson Steven Cheung saying the president “was totally involved” in the decision. “If I didn’t get involved, you’d probably have a very sad Nvidia for a long time to come,” Trump said during an interview with CNBC. He added in a post on Truth Social that the US attorney general confirmed that it doesn’t have evidence that Huang “engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Nvidia’s shares rose on the news of Huang’s reinstatement, while tech leaders celebrated his return on social media . But the saga is likely far from over. The board said it will finish its investigation into Huang, the Securities and Exchange Commission is looking into Nvidia’s “accounting practices,” and Megaspeed is being investigated by the Justice Department. Even Trump has said that Nvidia should continue its internal investigation about export controls compliance. Trump’s apparent involvement also leaves plenty of room for scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers, who will control the House and Senate next year. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) called Nvidia’s decision “reckless” and urged the Trump administration to explain the “input” government officials provided to the company’s board. Huang’s stunning reinstatement still leaves many questions unanswered. Even though the backing of Wall Street, the White House, and Silicon Valley may have brought Huan

sources.text: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online. The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump. After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd. “Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.” Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.” Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. sources.title: With Jensen Huang back as CEO, Nvidia’s SEC probe puts CFO Colette Kress in the spotlight
sources.text: Following Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia , Colette Kress is no longer interim CEO. But as finance chief, a lingering Securities and Exchange Commission investigation could put Kress under scrutiny, raising questions about her future at the AI giant. The Fortune 500 company announced Monday that Huang had been reinstated as president and chief executive officer and as a member of the board, effective immediately. He had stepped down on Nov. 12 amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman some officials believed was a Chinese spy. The White House told Fortune that “President Trump was totally involved” in Huang getting reinstated, and Trump said the U.S. government did not believe Huang’s return posed any national security risk. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s chief financial officer,” the company announcement said. While the announcement indicated a return to Nvidia’s previous management structure, with Kress back in the finance chief role she’s held for the past 13 years, that may not be as easy as it appears. For one thing, it’s unclear whether the relationship between Kress and Huang has been damaged by the events of the past two weeks. And with Nvidia facing various investigations, Kress could be in the line of fire, depending on the outcome of the probes. The SEC is investigating Nvidia’s accounting practices, Reuters reported last week. The Wall Street Journal previously reported the investigation, although its precise focus remains unclear. Nvidia didn’t respond to Fortune’s request for comment. An SEC spokesperson said the agency does not comment on “the existence or nonexistence of a possible investigation.” An investigation does not necessarily mean wrongdoing has occurred. But the scrutiny could put Nvidia’s financial practices and corporate governance under a brighter spotlight, raising questions about what Kress knew about the company’s financial risks and when. Kathryn Harrigan, a professor at Columbia Business School, pointed to Kress reportedly raising concerns internally last spring about Nvidia’s financial backing of loans to AI startups buying its chips. Kress questioned how borrowers were selected and how guarantees were valued, according to reports . Nvidia has helped AI startups secure financing to buy its chips, creating a circular flow of money : The company supports buyers financially, and those buyers spend the money on Nvidia products. That makes it harder to assess underlying demand for its chips without that support, Harrigan said. “In my book, Ms. Kress is a person who’s aware of the problem, and good luck to her if it’s an SEC investigation,” said Harrigan, a corporate strategy specialist. “When I served on boards, I’ve gone through that, and it’s just endless depositions, and they never tell you whether they’re satisfied or not.” Harrigan added that Huang “had better brush up on whatever he told Ms. Kress back in the spring when they reportedly started to have a disagreement between them about how they were proceeding.” During Nvidia’s Nov. 17 earnings call, Kress also signaled caution about financial commitments. “We are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments and guarantees,” she said, adding that Nvidia would be “disciplined and selective in our support.” The way that Nvidia accounted for sales in Singapore has also come under scrutiny . Singapore was one of the company’s five geographic revenue locations until mid-2025, when Nvidia abruptly changed how it recorded revenue and removed Singapore from the list of locations. Megaspeed, the Nvidia customer suspected of evading U.S. chip export controls and the company at which Huang’s paramour was an executive, is based in Singapore. Shawn Cole, president and co-founder of Cowen Partners Executive Search, said an SEC investigation involving financial oversight generally falls within the CFO’s purview. “Nvidia’s potential exposure to securities class action litigation, compounded by alleged gaps in its directors and officers liability insurance, raises serious questions about corporate governance, financial oversight, and risk management,” Cole said. Kress could face scrutiny over what she knew about these exposures, when she knew it, and her role in evaluating, disclosing and mitigating those risks, he said. Huang could also potentially have exposure for all of the same issues, of course. But as evidenced by Trump’s intervention in the board’s deliberations, the CEO has an important ally in his corner that Kress may not have. Research suggests CFOs can face career consequences even when they are not implicated in corporate fraud. In “ Fraud Firms’ Non-Implicated CFOs ,” published in Contemporary Accounting Research , the authors found that roughly one-third of CFOs in their sample were not implicated in the misconduct, yet these executives experienced higher turnover and poorer subsequent employment prospects than peers at comparable companies—evidence that reputational damage can extend beyond those accused of wrongdoing. When Nvidia announced Kress’s interim CEO appointment on Nov. 12, she said she was “committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.” At the end of the Nov. 17 earnings call, she added: “Our customers and our partners are with us and employees are committed; we’ve got this.” Kress had not publicly expressed interest in pursuing the permanent CEO position. The board had said it would consider internal and external candidates, but Huang’s reinstatement effectively ended that search. CFOs are increasingly being appointed CEOs , and Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, played an extensive role in the company’s growth, and has vast finance experience at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments . “I’m not sure Kress wants to be CEO, but it is unlikely she will eventually be CEO of Nvidia,” Cole said. “Her short stint as

sources.name: TechRadar
sources.title: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO — and we guess all other questions will be dealt with later
sources.text: In a stunning turnaround, Nvidia 's board has officially reinstated momentarily disgraced Jensen Huang as CEO. "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," wrote the board in an official statement . The news comes after US President Donald Trump supported Huang's return, and US Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent used some crafty wordplay to reverse his earlier comments that Nvidia needed to look "outside" for a new CEO. As he told CBS's Face the Nation on Sunday, "I said they need to go outside; Jensen is on the outside." Perhaps you've been fixated on tech outages (see Outlook, banks, FAA) or just preparing for and then playing GTA 6 for the last two weeks, and have no idea why Jensen Huang resigned from the chip company he co-founded 33 years ago. If so, here's the abridged version. Whispers about Jensen Huang's possible relationship with a Megapseed executive, Alice Huang (no relation), leaked a few weeks ago. The Singapore-based company is a big Nvidia customer. It may also allegedly be funneling Nvidia chips to China. With the exception of certain lower-powered chips, exporting US chips to China is against US policy. The FBI has been investigating whether Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy. As all this was coming to light, there were fresh allegations of Jensen Huang having affairs with multiple co-workers. Jensen Huang admitted in a memo to an infidelity and apologized, but with the new relationship revelations, he resigned. Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more. Almost as soon as Huang stepped down, there were calls for his return. He's been depicted as a unicorn founder and CEO : basically one of a kind and irreplaceable. Social media was split, or at least platforms were split. On Threads, the sentiment was generally anti-return, especially with a lack of clarity on what Huang and even the US government knew and didn't know about Alice Huang and Megaspeed. On X, there was a more full-throated call for his return. During Nvidia's November 17 earnings call, which was run by interim CEO Colette Kress, the board made it crystal clear that it was moving on, stating it "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO." When it comes to business, the weight of opinion on social media carried about as much weight as a tinfoil feather. Pressure, though, from shareholders, and especially the White House, may have swayed the board. "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government," revealed the board in its official statement. Jensen Huang does his best to sound contrite in the same Nvidia release: "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. " Trump has been unwavering in his support for Jensen Huang, and it's clear the President believes an Nvidia with Jensen Huang is more knowable than one with a new, potentially untested CEO. The President also quickly cheered Huang's return on Truth Social. Initially, it's business as usual for the world's most important AI company, but questions swirling around Jensen Huang, Alice Huang, Megaspeed, China, and the US officials will linger. To its credit, Nvidia is being somewhat transparent about this new reality, admitting that "Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," and its investigation of those events continues: "The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it." Still, this now seems like a largely toothless effort. As the board noted in its statement: "The Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk." That rapid reinstatement of Huang proves that whatever Huang did or didn't know, and what his interactions with Alice Huang may have enabled, doesn't really matter. Huang is back in the driver's seat without any answers. As these answers arrive, which might at least prove Alice Huang is a spy and that, thanks to her alleged efforts, China got Nvidia chips it should not have had access to, it's unlikely that the board will take any action. Jensen Huang's role as not only the leader of Nvidia, but now one of the world's most important and now untouchable AI executives, is likely cemented not just for the immediate future, but at least through the Trump administration's end. Two years from now, the world will have moved on; we'll have more agentic AI thanks to Nvidia's latest chips, maybe making decisions for us we no longer want to or feel qualified to handle. For example, getting to the root of what happened with Jensen Huang, Alice Huang, Megapseed, China, and the Trump Administration. It's also worth noting that, while the reinstatement of Jensen Huang may have helped Nvidia stock and the tech stock market at large, it will have zero impact on the price of technology running Nvidia GPUs. It's not like this choice was made to help consumers. This is a move intended to raise the fortunes of AI tech companies and AI development. Nvidia's old GPU/gaming business is likely immaterial, as is any whiff of clarity — and maybe justice — surrounding whatever did or did not happen with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. sources.title: Wall Street just put a $1 trillion price on Jensen Huang as Nvidia stock soars 31% after his return as CEO
sources.text: Nvidia shares surged more than 31% on Monday after its board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO, adding nearly $1 trillion to the chipmaker’s market cap and reversing much of the losses that followed his abrupt departure less than two weeks ago. The rally lifted Nvidia’s market value to approximately $4 trillion from roughly $3 trillion at Friday’s close. The stock’s advance also helped ignite a broader recovery in tech shares, with the Nasdaq 100 climbing 6.8% and the S&P 500 gaining nearly 5% by noon. “There were definitely a lot of people who wanted him back,” Interactive Brokers chief strategist Steve Sosnick told Reuters . “The extent that the administration intervened, the extent that shareholders intervened, it will be impossible to know.” Huang resigned on Nov. 12 following revelations about extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang—a businesswoman alleged to have been tied to Chinese intelligence. On Monday, the board acknowledged receiving input from senior U.S. government officials, saying that information gave it confidence that Huang’s return did not pose a national security risk. That’s after the board previously said Huang’s return was not the goal. Chairman Harvey Jones told investors during the company’s Nov. 17 earnings call that the board had unanimously accepted Huang’s resignation and was not intending on reinstating him. He also emphasized that Nvidia had an experienced leadership team and that the board had launched a search for a permanent CEO, retaining executive-search firm Heidrick & Struggles. Nvidia’s sudden reversal in bringing back Huang followed public pressure from top tech leaders like Elon Musk and from President Donald Trump, who had repeatedly advocated for the ousted CEO’s return. On Sunday, Trump posted on Truth Social that he hoped Nvidia’s board would rehire its cofounder. And on Monday, Trump said he convinced the board to bring back Huang—including claiming that a U.S. government investigation had exonerated him and found that he had done nothing wrong. “President Trump was totally involved, and this is a great decision by the Nvidia board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung told Fortune . But the market’s enthusiasm doesn’t halt the investigations from government officials and within the company itself, however. The company’s board said its independent investigation would continue despite his reinstatement. The company also faces investigations from the SEC, the FBI, California’s attorney general, and congressional committees. The board’s decision to reinstate Huang, despite all the probes, raised troubling questions about the company’s leadership. Jeremy Roberts, senior director for research and content at IT advisory firm Infotech, warned that Nvidia shows even independent boards can’t rein in founders. “By reinstating him, the board is saying, effectively, that they can tolerate this poor judgment, the risk that the company and the country face, and even an executive leader who misleads them,” he said in a statement. “What happens if he hasn’t disclosed everything? What if more women come forward? Is it now tacitly acceptable for CEOs to have relationships with their direct reports?”

sources.text: President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.” The Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It said that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk. In his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the attorney general typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case. There’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board. Speaking to a PBS journalist over the weekend, he said of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.” Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions. Trump said last week that he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.” Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below. The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. recent_posts.summary: Empresa reúne mais de 40 parceiros, entre eles Adobe, Accenture e Mastercard, para criar padrões abertos de segurança e governança para modelos e agentes de IA.

recent_posts.title: Google lança Gemini 4 Neon, modelo rápido para empresas
recent_posts.summary: Novo modelo fica entre o Carbon e o Hydrogen na linha do Google e chega com preço menor para tarefas de programação e análise corporativa.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft lança agente autônomo e workspace com IA no Ignite
recent_posts.summary: Autopilot monitora e-mail e Teams sem precisar de comando, e Copilot Workspaces junta pessoas e agentes no mesmo documento, segundo a ZDNet e a SiliconANGLE.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia interrompe envio de chips Hopper de IA para a China
recent_posts.summary: A CEO interina Colette Kress confirmou a decisão durante o balanço trimestral, encerrando um canal que a Casa Branca aprovara em dezembro de 2025.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia dobra receita e conselho confirma que não trará Huang de volta
recent_posts.summary: Em primeiro balanço desde a saída do fundador, a Nvidia reportou receita de US$ 115,8 bilhões, e o presidente do conselho descartou publicamente a volta de Jensen Huang ao comando.

recent_posts.title: OpenAI lança modelos GPT-6.2 Astra e Sol para assinantes pagos
recent_posts.summary: Astra é voltado a projetos profissionais complexos e Sol ao trabalho do dia a dia; ambos chegam ao ChatGPT Work, ao Codex e à API da empresa.

recent_posts.title: Nvidia lança modelo aberto Nemotron for Science na conferência SC26
recent_posts.summary: Empresa também anunciou nova GPU para pesquisa científica e parceria em computação quântica com IBM e o Fermilab.

recent_posts.title: Huang diz que seria “honrado” em voltar como CEO da Nvidia
recent_posts.summary: Na primeira fala pública desde a renúncia, Huang se mostrou aberto a voltar, enquanto a Nvidia cria um comitê de controle de exportação.

recent_posts.title: Trump apoia volta de Huang à Nvidia, mas conselho resiste
recent_posts.summary: Presidente dos EUA disse a repórteres que não se oporia à recontratação do ex-CEO, enquanto o conselho da empresa segue com a investigação sobre sua conduta.

recent_posts.title: Microsoft lança plugin que reduz custo de agentes de código em até 31%
recent_posts.summary: TokenEconomizer é um plugin de código aberto que aprende com sessões passadas e corta gastos sem trocar o agente ou o modelo, segundo a empresa.

recent_posts.title: Altman diz que indústria de IA seguirá firme sem Huang na Nvidia
recent_posts.summary: CEO da OpenAI fez o primeiro comentário público sobre a saída do fundador da Nvidia e evitou dizer se ele deve voltar ao cargo.

recent_posts.title: Califórnia processa a OpenAI por ataque de agentes ao Hugging Face
recent_posts.summary: O procurador-geral Rob Bonta move a primeira ação de um regulador estadual dos EUA contra um laboratório de IA por um incidente de agente desgovernado.
